# PedEdit

> PedEdit is a free, open-source pedigree editor for clinical genetics, genetic counselling and research, at https://pededit.com. It draws genetic family trees with the NSGC standard pedigree symbols and lays them out automatically with a TypeScript port of the kinship2 R package, so consanguinity, multiple partners and twins are drawn correctly. People can then be dragged to new places.

No account is needed. Creating a pedigree while signed out saves it on the server at its own link, https://pededit.com/p/<id>, and that link is the only key: anyone who has it can open and change the pedigree, so it should be bookmarked and shared with care. Signing in with Google or GitHub is optional and only adds a list of your pedigrees and a saved library of conditions and tags.

What it does:

- Draws NSGC symbols (Bennett et al. 2008 and the 2022 revision): affected and carrier status for several conditions in one chart, deceased, pregnancies and losses, adoption, twins, consanguinity, donors and surrogates, proband and consultand, gender identity.
- Imports PED files (the 6-column PLINK layout) and PedEdit JSON files.
- Exports PedEdit JSON (lossless), PED, CSV, SVG, PNG and PDF, with a de-identify option on the figure exports. Exports are made in the browser.
- Calculates kinship and inbreeding coefficients from the drawn family.

To hand a family to PedEdit, write it as a PedEdit JSON file (format below) or a PED file and import it from the home page with "Import from PED or JSON file".

Family histories are health information. Leave out names, dates of birth and other identifying details from anything you send through an assistant: a pedigree can be drawn with no names at all, and people can be named in PedEdit afterwards.

## Docs

- [PedEdit JSON format](https://pededit.com/docs/pedigree-json-format.md): every field of the pedigree data model, with the envelope a downloaded file uses
- [PedEdit JSON schema](https://pededit.com/docs/pedigree-json-schema.json): JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the same format

## Guides

- [Pedigree symbols cheat sheet](https://pededit.com/guides/pedigree-symbols): the NSGC 2022 symbols and lines, with the 2008 forms where they differ
- [How to draw a pedigree](https://pededit.com/guides/how-to-draw-a-pedigree): a three-generation pedigree step by step
- [Consanguinity in a pedigree](https://pededit.com/guides/consanguinity): the double line, and kinship and inbreeding coefficients for common relationships
- [Practice families for teaching](https://pededit.com/guides/practice-families): family histories to draw, with the answers

## Examples

Each link opens a built-in example in the editor. Nothing is saved until it is changed, and then it is saved as the visitor's own copy.

- [Three generations](https://pededit.com/example/three-generations)
- [Uncle-niece](https://pededit.com/example/uncle-niece)
- [Assisted reproduction](https://pededit.com/example/assisted-reproduction)
- [Queen Victoria, haemophilia B](https://pededit.com/example/queen-victoria)
- [Spanish Habsburgs](https://pededit.com/example/habsburgs)
- [Practice: cystic fibrosis, first cousin parents](https://pededit.com/example/practice-cystic-fibrosis)

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/SACGF/pededit): AGPL-3.0, with the layout engine under GPL-3.0. A team that must keep pedigrees on its own systems can run its own copy (INSTALL.md)
- [Changelog](https://pededit.com/changelog)
